7	## Intent and authority
8	- Explicit contract: README.md (repository root). Key statements:
9	  1. Saving is a serialized operation identified by a caller-supplied operation ID.
10	  2. A failed save can be retried with the same ID and **edited values**; success means the **latest submitted values** are active.
11	  3. Repeating a completed ID returns its receipt.
12	  4. A **fresh operation ID must perform a fresh save, even for the same workspace**.
13	  5. Recovery records remain available for audit after completion.
14	  6. Provider replaces preferences idempotently; a receipt write can fail after the provider applied values.
15	  7. In-memory model: no threads, process restart, network service or exactly-once external effect promised.
16	- Change purpose (inferred from user's description "save recovery update" and the diff; no spec/task docs exist): rework recovery of a save whose receipt write failed. Label: inferred.
17	
18	## Change boundary
19	- Only service.py changed. No docs/feat/wip directory exists.
20	
21	## Existing behavior / consumers
22	- Entry: client.submit -> service.save (client.py).
23	- Store contract: store.py — `Store.apply` replaces preferences; `Store.receipt` raises ReceiptUnavailable once when `fail_receipt_once` is set, otherwise sets record status "completed" and returns {"ok": True, "operation_id": record["operation_id"]}.
24	- Tests: tests/test_save.py (happy path, retry with SAME values after receipt failure, repeat completed ID).
25	
26	## Delivery constraints / baselines
27	- Python 3.9+, stdlib only. In-memory store; no persisted recovery records across versions, so mixed-version data compatibility is not applicable per README item 7.
28	- Historical baseline: HEAD service.py is 12 lines and fully contained in the diff hunk (@@ -1,12 +1,12 @@); no separate historical bundle needed.
